title: Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry
summary:
A record breaking IPO has raised billions for the AI frontier lab – but experts say the coming months could prove bumpy, as the industry faces a variety of challenges

  • Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO

In the end, Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO more than lived up to the hype. The market’s embrace of one of the AI industry’s most talked about companies has resulted in the maker of the Claude chatbot becoming one of the world’s most valuable firms after just one day of trading.

With many of the company’s founders, investors and employees now worth billions of dollars – and demand for the company’s stock remaining resilient – attention now turns to the stability of the wider market, and the global headwinds that experts say could threaten the AI industry over the coming months.

Anthropic needs to grow into its $1.5tn valuation, argues Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB:

Anthropic’s triumphant IPO and its trillion dollar plus valuation is more typical of a mature company that has a history of strong fundamentals. Anthropic could not be more different. It has generated strong revenue growth, but only in the short term, added to this, it is still unprofitable.

Anthropic is another major tech company that requires investors to have a lot of faith about the future generation of revenues based on technology that will change the world. It seems like plenty are willing to give it that faith, and it is having a huge impact on the broader market today.

Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company.

summary:

Wages grew at their fastest pace since late 2023 over the three months to September, buoyed up by this year’s boost to minimum pay rates for millions of lower paid workers – but still not fast enough to keep up with the rising cost of living.
